title: furrow epic shard v2
description: Schema for one .furrow/epics/<id>.json shard (a single epic: a box of work with member tasks). The board-wide schema_version lives in .furrow/meta.json, never in a shard. v2 is the board-layout v7 shape: the required deps set (the epic ids this box waits on — information, not enforcement; epic activate warns about an open dep and proceeds) plus the required standing/pinned declarations. Pin to a tagged URL or vendor this file.
$comment: true, deliberately: furrow PRESERVES top-level keys it does not know (a field written by a newer furrow that did not bump the layout version) and re-emits them on write, so a shard furrow itself produces may legitimately carry extras. Declaring them invalid here would make this artifact call furrow's own output non-conforming. Typo detection therefore lives in furrow lint, which warns unknown-shard-key (naming the epic) — nothing else can, since nothing ever deletes an extra.

id.description: frozen id, e- prefixed; == the shard filename stem and bodies/<id>.md stem

goal.description: the closing condition in one line. OPTIONAL in practice ("" is valid and never linted): a box whose title already says it gains nothing from restating it. Its value is that epic ls can show it.

active.description: this is the box currently being worked. At most one active epic per repo, and an epic naming several repos consumes a slot in each. furrow next scopes to it.

labels.description: free-form tags, same semantics as a task's

repos.description: repositories this box spans, owner/repo form, sorted+deduped. A repo-less epic cannot be activated (it would bypass the one-active-per-repo rule).

meta.description: free-form key/value furrow stores, round-trips and NEVER interprets. Flat (string values only) so the deterministic byte recipe holds: encoding/json sorts a map's keys, and a string cannot reintroduce float-precision churn. Not queryable by design — read it with jq.

closed.description: null while open; an epic has no lane — open/closed is its whole state model

body.description: relative path, e.g. bodies/e-k3m9.md — the SAME directory task bodies live in (ids are prefix-disjoint)

deps.description: epic ids this box waits on (open after those close), sorted+deduped, acyclic. Information, not enforcement: epic activate warns about a still-open dep and proceeds, a dep on a closed epic is satisfied, and revisit raises epic_dep_done when every dep is closed. furrow lint backstops the graph (epic-dep-cycle, epic-dep-missing, epic-dep-open).

standing.description: declares a PERMANENT box (an inbox-like channel, a parking lot): exempt from the finish-shaped revisit nags epic_all_done and epic_dep_done (epic_stuck still fires). furrow never interprets which boxes deserve it — that binding is the operator's convention.

pinned.description: the box's actionable tasks surface in next/brief REGARDLESS of the active-epic scope, at the top — an always-visible channel. Orthogonal to active and standing (a mandate box is standing+pinned; a parking lot standing only); needs no repo slot, the read's own repo filter scopes the tasks.

reviewed.description: when a human last re-assessed this box's contents (furrow review <epic-ref>, board layout v9); absent = never (which is why it is not in required). Tracked separately from updated (a review changes no content). Read by revisit's epic_review_due: a STANDING box whose last review is past [review].stale_after_days — the same clock as the per-repo review nudge — is due; a never-reviewed box stays quiet (the first review opts it in).
